title: Expire terminal ordinary Calibration runs
evidence_required: FT-011-AC-007 RED: terminal ordinary Calibration runs are absent from the existing 90-day cleanup; GREEN: diagnostics deletes only terminal runs strictly before the fixed cutoff, preserves equal/new terminal and active requested/running rows, leaves the public cleanup result unchanged and converges on rerun; decisive comparison: fixed-time disposable old/equal/new terminal plus active rows and latest-result state are inspected before cleanup, after cleanup and after one safe repeat; artifact: redacted destructive-probe output under .tasks/TASK-105-T3-FT-011-W2/.
purpose: Add terminal ordinary Calibration runs to the existing diagnostics cleanup step without another retention surface or lifecycle.
success_outcome: Terminal ordinary runs obey the existing strict-before 90-day cutoff while active/equal/new runs and the public cleanup result remain unchanged across safe rerun.
anti_goals: Do not implement staff promote/delete actions or modify promoted_subset behavior.
Do not add a cleanup command/timer, history/jobs/archive/tombstone table, Calibration-specific cutoff or public result count.
Do not delete promo-owned rows directly or touch production/operator state.

forbidden_scope: Production PostgreSQL/MinIO and operator/default Attempts, evidence or Calibration runs
Promoted-subset creation/deletion, staff Calibration actions and direct diagnostics deletion of promo rows
New scheduler/timer/history/archive state and changes to the public latest-cleanup result
stop_conditions: Terminal ordinary run expiry cannot reuse the existing diagnostics step and fixed 90-day cutoff without another cleanup surface.
Correct owner convergence requires a cross-owner cascade or changing existing event/Attempt/evidence/annotation ordering.
The destructive proof cannot use fixed-time disposable rows, one safe repeat, redacted artifacts and complete cleanup.

constraints: Extend the existing owner-ordered cleanup so diagnostics selects terminal ordinary Calibration runs strictly before the shared 90-day cutoff; active requested/running and equal/newer terminal rows are ineligible.
Keep the latest cleanup result shape unchanged and preserve existing event/Attempt/evidence/annotation deletion order and ownership.
Use fixed-time disposable rows, one safe repeat and complete task-owned cleanup.
invariants: Diagnostics deletes only its owned run rows and no ownership-crossing cascade or direct foreign write is introduced.
Cleanup never deletes active, equal-cutoff or newer runs and never changes serving state.
Repeated cleanup is safe and adds no lifecycle, history or public count.
verification_targets: Fixed-cutoff fixtures prove old terminal run deletion, equal/new terminal plus active-run preservation, unchanged public cleanup result and one safe rerun.
Ownership/source inspection proves reuse of the existing diagnostics cleanup step with no direct promo delete, cascade, extra timer/command/result field or archive/history model.
